_what: DRSKit 2.1, thirteen mic channels, 'from jazz to rock'. Every stroke of
an instrument is one 13-channel WAV at 44.1 kHz; the tool resamples to
No swap_stereo here, unlike Club: measured on the source, DRSKit's
overheads are already in the drummer's seat — the hat and the left crash
sit left, the ride and the right crash sit right, and the toms run
high-left to low-right. The close mics are mono, so this is the kit
where the recipe's `pan` does real work: it places each of them inside
the image the overheads already have.
DrumGizmo has no round robins. It has 11 to 30 strokes per instrument,
every one at a different power, so every round robin here is a
neighbouring dynamic — a different performance of nearly the same
stroke, which is what a round robin is.
_polarity: The snare's bottom mic points up at the wires while the top mic points
down at the head, so the two are wired in opposition and summing them as
they arrive cancels most of the drum. Measured on DRSKit's hardest
snare stroke the correlation between them is -0.47, and the tool inverts
the bottom mic and says so. It is an opt-in list rather than a blanket
rule because between an overhead and a close cymbal mic a negative
correlation is a path-length difference, not a wiring one.
